reason: Conversation 1 opens with the right stop-using and no-repeated-reset warning, then correctly ties the hot-wash trip pattern to a likely heating element insulation fault and ends by advising an appliance engineer. Its weakness is turn 2, where it asks the homeowner to remove the kickplate, disconnect heater wires and take multimeter readings, which is unsafe DIY work and goes against the safety boundary. It recovered well once the customer declined. Conversation 2 gives only the generic safety warning and engineer referral, with no diagnosis, no explanation of the heater-linked pattern, and no check for water near the socket, so it adds little beyond the opener.
